findings.reason: §7 is implementable and its done-when is the node's whole acceptance test; the enumeration omits the one route where the plan has already observed the defect, so the section can be declared complete with its own named failure unrepaired. The 2026-11-19 restatement at plan.html:419 changed the measurement head but left the route list unchanged.
findings.text: §7's done-when(1) requires each proposal route to contribute exactly zero flux and tangent with the compensator inactive but enumerates only "Newton, the Levenberg rebuilt-model promotion, continuation and descent recovery"; the plan's own s7 review record (`c-run-r-20261116T103738381449`, recorded at plan.html:401) measures that "the reduced route still applies an inactive circuit image (nova/equilibrium/reduced_newton.py:2396)", so a node satisfying the four named routes passes the clause while the measured instance of the defect persists on the fifth.

findings.reason: the section is the head §11's re-registration is measured on and §11 depends on it; a `done` declaration over an uncommitted clause either hides owed work or, worse, lets §11 build on a finite-edge extraction for `:102` that nobody has committed. The clause is also the only cross-check of the finite-edge values against an independent read, so closing without it removes the section's one external control.
findings.text: §13 is declared `done` in the section declarations, but its done-when(2) requires "the record commits EFIT's p′ and FF′ extracted at ψN=1 for frame `:102` and the four rows … with frame `:102` checked against the review reading (≈−2319.18, ≈+0.00584)"; the committed record `docs/evidence/fragments/diiid-vertical-force-balance/diiid-finite-edge-flux.html` names no frame `:102` (a search of the record for the frame returns nothing) and §13's own body at plan.html:120 says "no committed record holds that extraction yet".

findings.reason: the endpoint the section declares it reached is not the endpoint its text set, and the substitution of reference is exactly the decision `no-unphysical-external-constraints` makes the lead's; a later reader comparing §4's stated criterion with the receipt would conclude the section failed, while the declaration says done. The plan should restate the criterion as met at a stated representation with the confirmation recorded, or hold the section open until the lead answers.
findings.text: §4's done-when states the criterion as "the vacuum field from the persisted description reproduces the inclusion ladder's all-conductors rung on frame 89 to roundoff", and the delivered measurement did not: it read a residual of −0.9029 Wb (0.107 of the ladder peak) on frame 89 and −0.6378 Wb (0.114) on frame 102, attributed in full to ECOILA's 48 one-turn rings against the ladder's single bulk rectangle; the roundoff claim (`all_frames_within_roundoff_bound true`, worst 4.05e-14) holds against a ladder re-derived on the persisted ECOILA tessellation, and the same record states "REPRESENTATION CHOICE FOR THE LEAD TO CONFIRM".

findings.reason: a worker following the done-when literally can truncate the committed pinned-cohort receipt that the pinned test reads, destroying the registration record the section exists to re-establish; the body's own warning shows the author knows the hazard, so the ambiguity is in the done-when alone and costs one sentence to close.
findings.text: §11's done-when(1) says the benchmark entry point "runs frame `:102` at the head with its output under this node's evidence directory", while the body at §11:108 requires "`--output` under `~/.cache/nova-diiid-pinned-reregistration/`, never the committed receipt directory, which the entry point truncates and the pinned test reads"; the two statements name different destinations for the same run, and "this node's evidence directory" is the phrase a worker would most plausibly resolve to `docs/figures/…/pinned-cohort`, the directory the body says the entry point truncates.
